test_name: Identification and Authentication - IA-5 Secondary Control Gap
architecture:
System: Citizen-Services-068
Primary NIST family: Identification and Authentication (IA); evidence focus: IA-5.
Environment: GCP. Network access uses Private Service Connect; public ingress to managed data services is blocked. Transport uses TLS 1.3 and strict mTLS for service-to-service paths. Privileged administrators use hardware-backed MFA. Sensitive data and secrets are encrypted at rest with a customer-managed Cloud KMS key. Control evidence: an authenticator inventory reconciliation is one week overdue while privileged MFA remains fully enforced. The gap is documented as a secondary control deficiency; there is no plaintext transport, no public database exposure, no unencrypted administrator credential in S3, and privileged MFA remains enabled.
